Looking at the cuboid (5×2×2 = 20 cubes), the visible dark cubes are: three in a row along the bottom front, plus one on the top back at the right end of that row. The only hidden positions are the back‑bottom row, and for the dark piece to be connected, its fifth cube must be the hidden one directly behind the right end of the bottom row (below the visible top dark cube).

So the dark piece is: a row of 3 cubes, then one cube behind the end of the row, then one cube on top of that cube — a chain of 5 with two 90° turns (one horizontal, one vertical).

- Shapes A, B, C are flat (planar) — impossible.
- Shape D has a cube with three neighbors (a branch) — the dark piece is an unbranched chain — impossible.
- Shape E is exactly this chain: row of 3, turn up, turn back — which rotates to match row of 3, turn back, turn up.
